exposure: Use of antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) during pregnancy in women with epilepsy
cohort: A total of 120 pregnant women, comprising 60 with epilepsy using AEDs and 60 healthy controls, who gave birth at a specific Turkish medical center between April 2018 and April 2019.
finding: Epileptic pregnant women using AEDs had a significantly lower number of pregnancies per woman and higher rates of cesarean section deliveries and neonatal intensive care needs compared to healthy pregnant women.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section deliveries was statistically significantly higher in the epileptic group (68.3%) than in the control group (43.3%).
